provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The evaluator notes that the 'similar impacts on employer and non-employer firms' result raises the question of whether economic spillovers (job creation, networks) could be studied, e.g., using employer-employee matched PILA data; this is framed as an extension rather than a flaw.
issues.quote: I wonder if it would be possible to try to study some of these economic spillovers.

issues.text: In the panel specification, the non-PEP group shows a noticeable increase in entrepreneurship, which the evaluator finds unexplained; it is unclear whether something changed that could threaten the comparison.
issues.quote: It is not that clear to me why those who did not receive it see an increase (albeit much lower) in entrepreneurship (see figure 7). Did something change?

issues.text: The evaluator suggests an event study using visa receipt dates as a robustness check instead of the difference-in-differences design, implying the current panel approach is less informative about timing.
issues.quote: If there is also the date on where these persons received the visa, one could also use the panel data for an event study instead of a diff in diff, as a robustness check.

issues.text: Statistically significant treatment effects in later years (2021-2022) appear lagged relative to the policy, and the mechanism is unclear; the evaluator suspects COVID may be a confounder.
issues.quote: The treatment effect by year seems to be statistically significant until 2022 and 2021 (figure 6). I was wondering about the mechanism that might explain this lagged effect.

issues.text: Aggregate municipal-level effects on entrepreneurship are not examined; the evaluator notes that the results for native Colombian firms suggest no effect, which would need to be reconciled with any aggregate or indirect labor-market effects.
issues.quote: Although, given figure 6, it seems there is no effect for Colombian native firms.

issues.text: The instrument's construction could be improved: the evaluator suggests computing expected rather than only actual registration days by department, using the permutations, to address identification concerns in the related prior work.
issues.quote: One could compute not only the actual average registration days available by department but the expected one, using the same permutations done in the paper.

issues.text: The introduction's description of the decomposition into a physical relocation effect and a visa effect is ambiguous; the evaluator initially read relocation as movement between Colombian cities rather than from Venezuela to Colombia.
issues.quote: I firstly understood it as if the PEP-Pardon had an effect in migration towards different cities

issues.text: The assumptions are presented in general terms; the evaluator asks that each be linked directly to the study's context so readers can judge whether it holds and what threats exist.
issues.quote: It would be useful if at the end of each assumption, you could state for the case of the paper what would that mean directly.

issues.text: Results differ between the panel regression and the IV cross-section for the sub-samples in Tables 8 and 9, and the paper does not explain these differences.
issues.quote: Here, the results in the panel regression differs from the results using the IV cross-section. It would be important to explain these differences.

issues.text: The validity of the RD-based IV strategy is questioned because the compliers' PEP status is assumed sensitive to small timing differences; the evaluator finds it hard to believe that a window of more than two months versus slightly longer would matter so much.
issues.quote: This is the part of the paper that might be harder to believe. Even the people with a smaller time window had more than two months to get the PEP visa.

issues.text: The paper does not directly measure the time taken to obtain the PEP visa (days from process start to online submission), which the evaluator considers necessary to assess how much a week or two of extra window matters.
issues.quote: one thing that could help is if the document could talk about the time people took to obtain the PEP visa.
